source: Staged canonical Gilded Coast content pack, 2026-10-02

world.name: The Gilded Coast
world.description: An age-of-sail coast of bright harbors, working shipyards, dangerous privateers, intimate salons, and islands close enough to visit but far enough to keep their own rules.

locations.name: Admiralty Quay
locations.description: The working arrival edge of Tidemark, where law, labor, and departures share a narrow waterfront.

locations.name: Arrival Steps
locations.description: Passengers step from ferries into a crowded public landing where each arrival is announced by bell and chalk board.

locations.name: Customs House
locations.description: A tiled customs hall where manifests, licenses, and cargo seals determine who may unload.

locations.name: The Brass Compass
locations.description: A sailors’ tavern that serves hot breakfast before the first ferry and keeps a quiet back table for hard conversations.

locations.name: Ferry Hall
locations.description: A roofed waiting room for cay ferries, posted sailings, weather delays, and people who missed the last boat.

locations.name: Sailors’ Exchange
locations.description: Crews trade work notices, spare gear, and stories beneath an awning that smells of tar and coffee.

locations.name: Harbor Court
locations.description: A small open hearing room for berth disputes, salvage claims, and complaints against captains.

locations.name: Gilt Row
locations.description: Terraces, lenders, jewellers, and salons look over the same harbor that supplies their wealth.

locations.name: Pearl Salon
locations.description: An intimate music and debate room whose invitation list crosses class lines more often than its patrons admit.

locations.name: Salt Ledger Bank
locations.description: A lender’s elegant public room where ship finance becomes personal at the repayment desk.

locations.name: Gilt Auction Rooms
locations.description: Furniture, cargo lots, maps, and inherited valuables change hands before a crowd that knows their stories.

locations.name: Glass Garden
locations.description: A walled conservatory of shade plants and small tables above the noisy port.

locations.name: Velvet Balcony
locations.description: A balcony theatre where performers can be seen from the street before patrons hear them.

locations.name: Montrose Jewels
locations.description: A jeweller’s shop known for turning damaged sea finds into settings with visible repair seams.

locations.name: The Ropewalk
locations.description: The shipbuilding district is a place of skill, shared meals, labor politics, and constant repair.

locations.name: Shipwright Yard
locations.description: A busy open yard where hulls are built and arguments about safety travel faster than nails.

locations.name: Sail Loft
locations.description: A high-ceilinged loft where canvas is cut, patched, and stitched under daylight.

locations.name: Ropewalk Kitchen
locations.description: Workers and neighbors share hot meals at a long table after shifts that do not end together.

locations.name: Drydock Baths
locations.description: A modest bathhouse with separate quiet and social rooms for crews returning from work.

locations.name: Rivet School
locations.description: A working apprenticeship hall where young adults learn measurements, knots, and repairs from working crews.

locations.name: Lantern Foundry
locations.description: A small brass and glass workshop that supplies signal lamps and household lights.

locations.name: Lantern Market
locations.description: The crowded evening heart of Tidemark, where food, performance, pleasure, and neighborhood business overlap.

locations.name: Night Market
locations.description: Stalls sell food, cloth, charts, and gossip after the day crews finish work.

locations.name: Honeyglass Theatre
locations.description: A small performance house where musicians, dancers, and storytellers work for an audience close enough to answer back.

locations.name: House of Hours
locations.description: A worker-run adult companionship house with a public tea room and private rooms governed by clear individual boundaries.

locations.name: Mariner’s Table
locations.description: A lively kitchen where fishers, captains, and market workers all want the last bowl of stew.

locations.name: Blue Lantern Inn
locations.description: An inn with plain rooms, good locks, and a front desk used to welcoming people who do not want questions.

locations.name: Spice Courtyard
locations.description: A public courtyard where street food, chess, and small music sets share the evening shade.

locations.name: Breakwater Point
locations.description: Storm watchers, healers, and guards work where the harbor meets open water.

locations.name: Lightkeep
locations.description: The lighthouse keeper’s work rooms and public viewing stair overlook the dangerous outer approach.

locations.name: Storm Clinic
locations.description: A small coastal clinic where injuries, seasickness, and lost sleep arrive with the tide.

locations.name: Battery Yard
locations.description: A working fort yard used for drills, repairs, and occasional public ceremonies.

locations.name: Tide Observatory
locations.description: A weather and tide station where handwritten records matter more than confident predictions.

locations.name: Breakwater Steps
locations.description: Wide public steps where residents watch departures or sit with the noise of waves.

locations.name: Signal House
locations.description: The flag room sends warnings and harbor permissions across a coastline with no instant messages.

locations.name: The Outer Cays
locations.description: Nearby islands and reefs depend on Tidemark but keep their own schedules, councils, and loyalties.

locations.name: Reef Landing
locations.description: A small ferry pier where island residents unload fish and visitors learn that the last return is tide-dependent.

locations.name: Coconut Beach
locations.description: A sheltered public beach with shade, shallow water, and enough room for quiet company.

locations.name: Tidepool Cove
locations.description: A low rocky shore where children and researchers watch the water withdraw and return.

locations.name: Windward Village
locations.description: A fishing village with a school, net sheds, shared kitchen, and a council that does not speak with one voice.

locations.name: Blackfin Anchorage
locations.description: A sheltered cove used by independent captains whose repair work is legal even when their last voyage is disputed.

locations.name: Sable Reef
locations.description: A shallow reef with a marked safe channel and a disputed boundary between fishing and salvage.

characters.name: Captain Elara Voss
characters.biography: Elara won her charter by taking a raider alive, then lost three crew in a later fight she chose to press. She pays the survivors’ families and refuses to let that settle what happened.

characters.name: Tomas Renn
characters.biography: Tomas stopped a quay riot without firing a shot, then signed an arrest order he now doubts. He keeps the harbor safe while privately questioning whom its rules protect.

characters.name: Anika Saye
characters.biography: Anika rose through the customs office by noticing what others called harmless exceptions. She has learned that a perfect record can conceal a cruel decision.

characters.name: Rafiq Nadir
characters.biography: Rafiq learned the channels from his mother and kept the cay ferry running through two contested seasons. He smiles easily until someone treats island passengers as spare cargo.

characters.name: Mira Cael
characters.biography: Mira learned flag codes while working night watches. Her accuracy made her useful to captains who rarely asked whether she wanted their secrets.

characters.name: Nico Solari
characters.biography: Nico carries messages and small parcels between offices that mistrust one another. He is good at being liked and tired of being trusted only with errands.

characters.name: Seraphine Vale
characters.biography: Seraphine inherited ships and debts together. She funds rescue work that her critics call a cheap way to keep control of captains.

characters.name: Julian Mercer
characters.biography: Julian can calculate risk better than he can explain why he keeps making exceptions for familiar families. A generous loan once cost him a colleague’s trust.

characters.name: Sabine Quill
characters.biography: Sabine earned her first property through companionship work and now runs a salon that pays performers by name. She resents being called an exception to a trade that supported her.

characters.name: Lucien Damar
characters.biography: Lucien performs for nobles and dockworkers, but the tune everyone requests was built with a singer who never received credit. He wants the truth on the next program.

characters.name: Iria Montrose
characters.biography: Iria repairs heirlooms without hiding the seam. A wealthy client once accused her of devaluing a piece by telling its owner what the stone had survived.

characters.name: Hugo Fen
characters.biography: Hugo has kept a wealthy household working through funerals, births, and a failed harvest. His own family sees him most often when another family is away.

characters.name: Bruna Kest
characters.biography: Bruna rebuilt ferries after the great storm and knows exactly which timber substitutions saved time. She has spent years correcting other people’s plans and wants an understudy she can trust.

characters.name: Mateo Salt
characters.biography: Mateo inherited a pattern book from his father and an unpaid invoice from the same voyage. He is inventive with cloth and evasive with lenders.

characters.name: Yara Nouri
characters.biography: Yara learned knots on her family’s fishing boat and joined the formal school to earn work beyond the cays. She wants credit as a rigger, not praise for being brave.

characters.name: Dorian Pike
characters.biography: Dorian fought under a pirate flag and struck a boarding officer he still believes was unarmed. He has built safer ships for years but has never given the officer’s family his account.

characters.name: Levi Ash
characters.biography: Levi makes rope that ships depend on but sees his name disappear behind a yard stamp. He jokes while negotiating and later regrets how much he gives away.

characters.name: Celia Mar
characters.biography: Celia organized meal and wage ledgers during a storm season. She can speak for a crowd and sometimes forgets to ask whether its quietest members agree.

characters.name: Inez Sol
characters.biography: Inez works at the House of Hours and performs onstage by choice. A patron who admired her dancing now assumes he owns the story of her career.

characters.name: Cassia Bloom
characters.biography: Cassia runs the Blue Lantern Inn with excellent locks and careful staff handovers. Her discretion has helped guests and hidden one debt she should have disclosed.

characters.name: Luca Vane
characters.biography: Luca chooses clients and singing engagements separately. He resents patrons who treat payment as a right to his private history and friends who assume the work prevents real ambition.

characters.name: Fen Moreno
characters.biography: Fen can mend a stage in the morning and make it sound alive at night. They want credit for arranging music that audiences attribute to the headliner.

characters.name: Javier Ro
characters.biography: Javier fed crews on credit during a lean season and still keeps the ledger, though he dislikes what it implies. He knows food is comfort and also a business with wages.

characters.name: Maia Bel
characters.biography: Maia’s act depends on trust and precise rehearsal. A patron wants a more dangerous trick because he mistakes real risk for excitement.

characters.name: Dr. Amara Kade
characters.biography: Amara treats injuries without asking a flag’s color first. A pirate she saved once returned with a crew harmed by the same conflict; neutrality now feels less simple.

characters.name: Bastien Crow
characters.biography: Bastien led a boarding that killed two raiders and saved a captured crew. He will defend the decision in public but knows the casualty report names people, not symbols.

characters.name: Talia Wren
characters.biography: Talia kept the light through a storm while the town called her heroic; she was mostly frightened and well trained. She wants colleagues credited for work done out of view.

characters.name: Oren Gale
characters.biography: Oren’s storm warnings are respected because he records his misses. He once delayed an alarm to confirm a reading and has never stopped calculating the cost.

characters.name: Nera Tide
characters.biography: Nera has recovered cargo and bodies from the same wreck. She wants salvage work to pay fairly without turning every found object into someone else’s prize.

characters.name: Sami Haddad
characters.biography: Sami can find a missing powder keg faster than most officers can name a guard shift. He dislikes how often the safest choice is hidden behind a tidy inventory.

characters.name: Captain Mara Blackfin
characters.biography: Mara took an Admiralty patrol cutter in Year 91; people died and the stories still disagree about who fired first. She protects cay families fiercely and refuses to be called innocent.

characters.name: Idris Vale
characters.biography: Idris moves goods across taxes he considers predatory. His cousin Seraphine financed his first boat and now expects a ledger he cannot provide without exposing friends.

characters.name: Sora Bay
characters.biography: Sora fishes before council meetings and knows exactly how city timetables erase island work. She can compromise on price but not on who gets to speak for her neighbors.

characters.name: Keon Flint
characters.biography: Keon has guided ships through channels that change after every storm. He loves the skill and resents captains who treat his knowledge as a temporary expense.

characters.name: Nadia Storm
characters.biography: Nadia left a comfortable city apprenticeship to learn live reefs. She wants independent certification and hates that a single mistake is remembered longer than her good routes.

characters.name: Elias Reed
characters.biography: Elias teaches charts, letters, and tide sense to island families. His former students now argue with him in council, which is exactly what he hoped would happen.
